title: Disjoint Sets
description: Learn the union-find data structure, path compression, and union by rank for efficient set grouping.

data.text: A disjoint-set, also called union-find, tracks a collection of non-overlapping sets. It answers two questions quickly: 'Are these two items in the same set?' and 'Can we merge these two sets?' This makes it invaluable for problems involving connectivity, grouping, and minimum spanning trees.

Imagine each item starts in its own singleton set. The find operation tells you which set an item belongs to by following parent pointers until it reaches a root. The union operation merges two sets by linking one root under the other.

data.title: Union-Find in JavaScript
data.content: A basic union-find implementation with path compression and union by rank.

data.title: Union-Find optimizations
items: Path compression flattens the tree during find by pointing each visited node directly to the root.
Union by rank always attaches the smaller tree under the larger one, keeping the tree shallow.
Together these optimizations bring the amortized cost per operation close to O(alpha(n)), where alpha is the inverse Ackermann function and is effectively constant for all practical sizes.

data.title: Amortized near-constant time
data.text: With path compression and union by rank, a sequence of m operations on n elements runs in almost linear time. This is one of the rare cases where a simple data structure achieves remarkable efficiency.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Union-find tracks which items belong to the same group.
Find locates the root; union merges two groups.
Path compression and union by rank are essential optimizations.
It is the standard tool for cycle detection and connectivity problems.
data.takeaway: Disjoint sets turn the question 'are these things connected?' into an almost instantaneous answer.
